reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Moses' divorce law as already inclining toward Jesus' teaching, so Deuteronomy's permission never licensed what Luke condemns.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll noted Christ's divorce ruling brands remarriage adultery, straining against the Mosaic permission Deuteronomy grants.

quotes.text: There is nothing on that subject in the new Testament; besides, Christ did apparently allow divorce, for one cause at least. He is reported to have said: "Whosoever putteth away his wife, save for fornication, causeth her to commit adultery."
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (1881), "Divorce," on Deuteronomy 24:1-2 and Luke 16:18.

sides.snippet: When she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man's [wife].
sides.verseText: When she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man's [wife].

sides.snippet: Everyone who divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.
sides.verseText: Everyone who divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.
